title: Deployment, Reliability, and Maintenance
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terms of deployment, reliability, and maintenance.
Apply development, staging, and production schemas in a small PostgreSQL-oriented example or design decision.
Validate the result against the expected behavior and identify one portability, safety, or edge-case consideration.

content.intro: Learn deployment, reliability, and maintenance through a short explanation, a concept diagram, and a PostgreSQL-oriented example. Focus on the reason for the query or design decision before memorizing syntax.
content.why_it_matters: Deployment, Reliability, and Maintenance matters because database behavior becomes more reliable when the intended row meaning, data shape, and edge cases are explicit. This lesson follows the SQL curriculum's listed subtopics and calls out PostgreSQL-specific behavior when it matters.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Professional work with deployment, reliability, and maintenance means that another person can review, repeat, and safely operate the query. Keep formatting consistent, test meaningful edge cases, use versioned migrations, and document engine/version assumptions.

content_blocks.title: Apply the idea
content_blocks.text: Start with the subtopics: Development, staging, and production schemas, Applying migrations safely, Backup and recovery concepts, Monitoring query behavior. Define the result you expect, run or inspect the small example in your own disposable PostgreSQL lab, and change one assumption at a time. The embedded lesson editor is a demonstration shell: the current project shows the sample expected output and does not execute arbitrary SQL on the server.

items.title: Development, staging, and production schemas
items.text: Development, staging, and production schemas changes how data is represented or exposed. Check dependencies, name objects consistently, keep structural changes in reviewed migrations, and rehearse the operation against a disposable copy before production.

items.title: Applying migrations safely
items.text: Applying migrations safely makes SQL easier to change safely. Turn assumptions into repeatable checks, keep schema/query changes reviewable, use deterministic ordering, and record the data shape and environment used for the check.

items.title: Backup and recovery concepts
items.text: Backup and recovery concepts helps you build professional workflows for SQL style, static analysis, tests, migrations, application integration, connection pooling, and pagination. Start with a concrete example, state the expected result, and verify the behavior before extending the query or design.

items.title: Monitoring query behavior
items.text: Monitoring query behavior helps you build professional workflows for SQL style, static analysis, tests, migrations, application integration, connection pooling, and pagination. Start with a concrete example, state the expected result, and verify the behavior before extending the query or design.

items.title: Schema compatibility during application releases
items.text: Schema compatibility during application releases changes how data is represented or exposed. Check dependencies, name objects consistently, keep structural changes in reviewed migrations, and rehearse the operation against a disposable copy before production.

items.title: Documentation and operational handover
items.text: Documentation and operational handover begins with a definition of the metric and its grain. Name the numerator, denominator, time zone, null policy, and tie-handling rule before translating the definition into SQL.

content_blocks.code:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(total_amount), 0) AS total_amount
FROM orders;
content_blocks.expected_output: The result reports the number of orders and a total amount, using zero for an empty sum only for display.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run in a disposable local PostgreSQL database such as codeleaf_sql_lab after loading datasets/postgresql-lab-setup.sql. Do not use production credentials or a production database. Some specialist examples require optional extensions or a specific PostgreSQL version, as stated in the lesson. The CodeLeaf lesson Run button in this scaffold only previews the documented expected output; it is not a SQL execution service.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For queries, restore the original text and compare results. For statements that change data, use the transaction and rollback shown in the example, or recreate the disposable lab from the included setup instructions. Do not reset production data.

content_blocks.title: Remember
content_blocks.text: SQL correctness depends on data shape, constraints, NULL behavior, row counts, and the target database dialect—not just whether a statement parses.

content.task: Try it yourself: demonstrate deployment, reliability, and maintenance using the sample schema. State what each returned row represents, test one edge case related to the lesson, and record the result.
task_acceptance_criteria: The query or design example matches the lesson's intended behavior.
The expected row grain and relevant NULL, duplicate, boundary, or permission behavior are explained.
The test is performed only in the local disposable lab, or clearly marked as a static inspection when a real runner is unavailable.
hints: Begin with the subtopic development, staging, and production schemas and write down the result you expect.
Use the smallest valid example; verify table and column names before adding complexity.
Inspect one edge case: missing values, duplicate matches, tied sort values, a constraint violation, or an engine-specific syntax difference.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a query is correct because it returns some rows.
common_mistakes.why: A result can omit valid records, multiply joined rows, mishandle NULLs, or rely on a non-deterministic order.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected row grain, add targeted edge cases, and use a stable tie-breaker whenever order or pagination matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying PostgreSQL syntax into another SQL engine without checking support.
common_mistakes.why: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, and Oracle differ in types, functions, row limits, procedural features, and transaction behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Label the target engine/version and verify the relevant official reference before adapting the query.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing with production data or credentials.
common_mistakes.why: Practice statements can change rows or expose sensitive information if run against the wrong connection.
common_mistakes.fix: Use a dedicated disposable lab, check current_database() and current_user, and review all changes before committing.

summary: Deployment, Reliability, and Maintenance is about making the database behavior and the expected result explicit.
Use the provided subtopics as a review checklist and validate a small test case.
Keep vendor-specific syntax, access assumptions, and production-safety boundaries visible.
